items.title: Hike the Petrified Forest
items.summary: The petrified forest trail is a remote and beautiful hike, leading to a dramatic landscape of petrified stumps and layered buttes.
items.durationNote: Hiking just to the petrified forest (either section) is a 3-mile out-and-back hike. The entire loop is 10.4 miles.

image.alt: A large petrified stump is central to the image, with others and large buttes visible behind it.

items.title: Hike Skyline Vista Trail
items.summary: Skyline Vista Trail is a great accessible introduction to Theodore Roosevelt National Park.
items.durationNote: The Skyline Vista Trail is a 0.1 mile round-trip accessible hike to an overlook with seating.

image.alt: A trailhead sign next to a paved trail in a grassy area. Buttes are visible on the horizon.

items.title: Birding in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
items.summary: The badlands of North Dakota are home to more than 180 species of birds. Take a moment and see which ones you can spot!

image.alt: A yellow breasted bird with brown wings and head sings at the top of a tree with needles.

items.title: Wildlife Viewing - South Unit
items.summary: Explore the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park and see the wide variety of wildlife that lives there.

image.alt: A group of bison cross a butte, the badlands dim behind them.

items.title: Wildlife Viewing - North Unit
items.summary: Explore the North Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park and see the wide variety of wildlife that lives there.

image.alt: A group of bighorn sheep cross a hillside above a bison.

items.title: Visit the Elkhorn Ranch Unit
items.summary: Visit the location of Theodore Roosevelt's home ranch, the Elkhorn, and experience the solitude of the North Dakota badlands.
items.durationNote: The Elkhorn Ranch Unit is remote, located between the North and South units. Visitors should plan for a drive of approximately 90 minutes each way, with time to hike and explore at the Elkhorn unit itself.

image.alt: A black and white photo of a low ranch house, with a porch. Elk antlers hang on the walls.
image.credit: Historic photo taken by Theodore Roosevelt

items.title: Hike Coal Vein Trail
items.summary: Take a hike on this 0.8-mile loop and learn about the geology of Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

image.alt: A trail winds through low buttes under a blue sky, with grass and flowers growing around it.

items.title: Hike Wind Canyon Trail
items.summary: Wind Canyon trail is a short, moderate-difficulty trail that rewards hikers with incredible views of the Little Missouri river and the surrounding badlands.
items.durationNote: The Wind Canyon trail is a 0.3 mile loop, with scenic views along its length.

image.alt: A bend in the river and a trail above it are seen at sunset. Buttes and prairies line the river.

items.title: Hike Boicourt Trail
items.summary: This short hike, with its elevated perspective and accessible trail, offers a unique view of the Little Missouri Badlands that the whole family can enjoy.

image.alt: The badlands, including a view down into a sandy bottomed valley and large buttes under a cloudy sky

items.title: Visit Theodore Roosevelt's Maltese Cross Cabin
items.summary: The Maltese Cross Cabin was Theodore Roosevelt's first home in Dakota territory. Step inside and learn about how he lived during his time in the badlands where the romance of his life began.

image.alt: A log cabin sits in a grassy area on the other side of a wooden fence, trees and blue sky behind it.

items.title: Hike The Little Mo Nature Trail
items.summary: Take a short hike along the Little Mo Nature Trail and learn about the nature and geology of Theodore Roosevelt National Park!

image.alt: A paved trail leads to a bridge over a creek. A picnic shelter is seen behind some trees.

items.title: Watch the Theodore Roosevelt National Park Film: Refuge of the American Spirit
items.summary: Visit one of the visitor centers and watch the Theodore Roosevelt National Park film, Refuge of the American Spirit.

image.alt: The sun is just visible over a badlands scene. Juniper grow on the buttes, and there are low clouds.

items.title: Hike up Buck Hill
items.summary: Hike to the top of Buck Hill, one of the highest points in the park, and get an amazing 360° view of the surrounding badlands!

image.alt: Two children sit on the edge of a rock ledge and gaze out over the badlands, juniper, and trails.

items.title: Bike the South Unit Scenic Drive
items.summary: Hop on your mountain bike and experience the South Unit Scenic Drive in a whole new way.

image.alt: A road curves to the left, with yellowing trees on both sides. Large buttes are in the distance.

items.title: Bike the North Unit Scenic Drive
items.summary: Bike the 14-mile scenic drive of Theodore Roosevelt National Park's remote North Unit!

image.alt: A road winds past buttes, viewed from above.

items.title: Hike the Painted Canyon Nature Trail
items.summary: Painted Canyon Trail is a 1-mile loop trail located just off Interstate 94 near the Painted Canyon Visitor Center. It offers a great introduction to Theodore Roosevelt National Park, whether visitors are just passing through or planning on a multi-day stay.

image.alt: A view up a trail towards a butte through junipers. A trail marker reads Painted Canyon.

items.title: See the Stars in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
items.summary: Theodore Roosevelt National Park offers incredible night skies for amateur and expert stargazers alike to enjoy year round.

image.alt: A ranger stands with several people, pointing a green laser at the sky. Stars are visible above them

items.title: Drive the South Unit Scenic Drive
items.summary: The South Unit scenic drive is the gateway to the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

image.alt: A photo taken from road level. Two yellow lines travel out of sight, with buttes in the distance.

items.title: Drive the North Unit Scenic Drive
items.summary: The North Unit scenic drive provides access to the more rugged North Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

image.alt: A road curves out of sight around some buttes. Yellowish grass grows on both sides of the road.

items.title: Become a Theodore Roosevelt National Park Junior Ranger
items.summary: Visit one of the park's visitor centers to pick up a Junior Ranger Field Journal, and start your journey to becoming a Junior Ranger!

image.alt: Two women smiling at the camera, one in a ranger uniform, holding a junior ranger book and badge.

items.title: Explore the Cannonball Concretions
items.summary: The cannonball concretions are an arresting and unusual geological formation. Stop at this pullout to explore their mysteries!
items.durationNote: The cannonball concretions are contained to a relatively small area, though there is access to the Buckhorn trail at this pullout.

image.alt: Several large round rocks eroded out of the side of a butte. The sky above the butte is cloudy blue.

items.title: Hiking in the South Unit
items.summary: From paved paths to strenuous backcountry trails – the hiking trails in the South Unit have a little something for everyone. Explore a sampling of park terrain with trail options to fit all levels of hikers.

image.alt: Sunshine highlights slopes on rolling badlands landscape.

items.title: Hiking in the North Unit
items.summary: Nature Trails in the North Unit are perfect for casual hikers and nature enthusiasts, but the backcountry trails really steal the show! The Buckhorn, Caprock Coulee, and famed Achenbach Trails traverse the park's vast wilderness areas. Check out all the options and what will fit your trip best.
items.durationNote: Variable; each trail listing includes mileage and terrain description to assist the visitor in calculating how long it would take to complete.

image.alt: Landscape view of dramatic Badlands with prominent coal seam.
